name: Workshop - Cedar Health (Readmission Risk & Intervention)
narrative:
Dr. Alicia Wren, a non-technical VP of Population Health, opens her care-coordinator panel and sees what her coordinators have been sensing for three weeks: a cluster of recently-discharged heart-failure patients glowing red — rising 30-day readmission risk driven by post-discharge care gaps a batch report surfaces too late to act on. Each avoidable readmission costs ~$15K and puts Medicare reimbursement at risk.

She asks about the highest-risk patient: PT-0000214, discharged eight days ago after a heart-failure admission, no completed follow-up, a medication-adherence flag, and a readmission-risk score of 0.88 — which intervention should the team run, and can they absorb it? The assistant ranks the three plays (a 7-day follow-up call, a medication reconciliation, or a home-health referral), each with projected readmission-risk reduction, cost, and the load it adds against the coordination team's current capacity, from a heuristic scored on Cedar's own intervention history. It recommends the follow-up call, drafts the care-plan summary, and stops for approval. Dr. Wren approves; the assignment writes back to Lakebase with an audit trail — governed clinical data turned into a coordinator action, PHI kept inside the governed boundary with no egress, and the assistant's AI spend capped and observable on thin operating margins.

Workshop training template (Tech Summit FY27 Live Days): data generator + full spec set (SDP pipeline, metric views, intervention model, dashboard + Genie, and a Databricks App with a Visualize/Assist/Act agent loop over Lakebase). Maps to the three build milestones — Lakebase, Databricks Apps, Unity AI Gateway.
